examples.en: This product was certified as safe.
When the account is verified, you get a text message.
Only verified shops appear in the app.
You get verified only after your identity is confirmed.
It's a site that hasn't been verified yet.
I'll wait until it's certified by an official body.

explain: 제품, 계정, 가게가 믿을 만하다고 확인받았을 때 써요. 앱이나 사이트에서 '인증 완료', '인증 번호'처럼 아주 자주 보여요. 사람의 실력을 인정받을 때는 '인정되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: This shop received a hygiene certification.
phrases.nuance_ko: 확인을 받는 쪽에서 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used from the side being certified.

phrases.en: Please enter the verification code from the text message.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앱이나 사이트에서 아주 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Seen very often in apps and websites.

phrases.en: The account hasn't been verified yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 확인이 끝나지 않았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the check isn't finished yet.

explain_en: Used when a product, account, or shop is officially confirmed as trustworthy. You see it constantly in apps, like 인증 완료 or 인증 번호. For a person's ability being recognized, use 인정되다 instead.

en: to get; to acquire; to come by

examples.ko: 경찰이 사건 영상을 입수한 뒤 조사를 시작했어요.
examples.en: The police began investigating after obtaining the footage of the incident.
I lined up from morning to get hold of a ticket.
Where did you get that news?

examples.ko: 새 정보를 입수하면 바로 알려 드릴게요.
examples.en: If I get new information, I'll let you know right away.

examples.ko: 귀한 책을 겨우 입수했는데 너무 낡았어요.
examples.en: I finally got hold of a rare book, but it's very worn.
It's hard to get hold of, so it's expensive.

explain: '얻다'나 '구하다'보다 딱딱하고, 정보나 자료, 귀한 물건을 손에 넣었다는 느낌이 강해요. 뉴스에서 '영상을 입수했다'처럼 자주 들려요. 선물을 받거나 밥을 먹을 때는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: The reporter got hold of secret information.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자료나 정보를 손에 넣을 때 가장 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The collocation that best fits getting hold of data or information.

phrases.en: News has just come in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정보나 자료가 손에 들어온 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes information or material having come into one's hands.

phrases.en: I had a hard time finding an old photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 쉽고 일상적으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but easier and more everyday.

explain_en: It is stiffer than 얻다 or 구하다 and stresses getting hold of information, materials or a rare item. You often hear it in the news, as in '영상을 입수했다'. It is not used for receiving a gift or having a meal.

dis.h: formal; obtain information or goods through channels
gh: get something from someone, often free

p.n: The swap is grammatical but plainer, and it loses the sense of acquiring through official or special channels.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 우리 동네 대표 맛집으로 자리매김했어요.
examples.en: This shop has established itself as our neighborhood's signature restaurant.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 믿고 듣는 가수로 자리매김하고 있어요.
examples.en: That singer is establishing herself as an artist you can trust.

examples.ko: 새 앱이 시장에서 자리매김하려면 시간이 필요해요.
examples.en: It takes time for a new app to establish itself in the market.

examples.ko: 이번 전시회가 문화 행사로 자리매김하기를 바라요.
examples.en: I hope this exhibition becomes an established cultural event.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 자리매김은 아직 분명하지 않아요.
examples.en: That company's position is still not clear.

examples.ko: 노력 끝에 주전 선수로 자리매김한 그는 인터뷰에서 웃었어요.
examples.en: After hard work, he settled in as a starter and smiled in the interview.

explain: 주로 '~로 자리매김하다' 형태로 써서 사람, 가게, 상품, 행사가 좋은 위치를 얻었다는 긍정적인 뜻이에요. '자리 잡다'와 비슷하지만 뉴스나 기사에서 더 격식 있게 쓰여요.

phrases.en: This song has established itself as a national favorite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '자리매김'에 '하다'를 붙여 실제 문장에서 가장 많이 쓰는 동사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form with '하다', the most common way to use it in real sentences.

phrases.example: 그 축제는 지역 대표 행사로 자리매김되었어요.
phrases.en: That festival has been established as the region's signature event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로가 아니라 사람들에게 인정받아 자리 잡은 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense of being recognized by others rather than doing it oneself.

phrases.en: The brand succeeded in establishing its position in the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 위치를 얻는 데 성공했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone succeeded in gaining a good position.
phrases.en_equiv: to succeed in establishing a position

explain_en: It is mostly used as '~로 자리매김하다' with a positive meaning that a person, shop, product or event has won a good position. It is similar to '자리 잡다' but sounds more formal and appears often in news articles.

examples.ko: 그 일은 알고 보니 본인의 자작극이었어요.
examples.en: It turned out that the whole thing was staged by the person himself.
There was a person who staged a stunt to become famous.
It came out that the theft report was a hoax.

examples.ko: 이 소문이 자작극 아니냐는 의심도 나와요.
examples.en: Some people suspect this rumor is staged.
The hoax was exposed, so he posted an apology.
I was fooled by my friend's setup and worried for a long time.

explain: 스스로 일을 꾸며 놓고 남이 한 것처럼 보이게 하는 일에 써요. '자작극을 벌이다, 꾸미다'로 자주 말하고, 뉴스나 SNS에서 '자작극 논란'처럼 나와요.

phrases.en: He staged a hoax to get attention.
phrases.nuance_ko: 없던 일을 일부러 만들어 낸다는 느낌으로, '자작극'과 가장 자주 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense of deliberately making up something that did not happen; a very common pairing with 자작극.

phrases.en: That incident got caught up in a controversy over whether it was staged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 SNS에서 사실인지 의심받을 때 제목처럼 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used like a headline when people doubt something is real.

phrases.en: The theft turned out to be staged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 뒤에 진짜가 아니라고 드러났을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an investigation shows something was not real.
phrases.en_equiv: to turn out to be staged

explain_en: It refers to staging something yourself and making it look like someone else's doing. Common phrases are '자작극을 벌이다/꾸미다', and '자작극 논란' appears often in news and social media.

examples.en: The police decided to investigate the cause of the accident again.
The test results looked odd, so I asked for a re-investigation.

examples.ko: 이 사건은 재조사 끝에 다른 결론이 나왔어요.
examples.en: After a re-investigation, this case reached a different conclusion.
I heard the school started a re-inspection of meal hygiene.
I heard the re-investigation results come out next month.
Residents want the construction site to be re-examined.

explain: 처음 조사가 부족했거나 결과를 믿기 어려울 때 다시 조사하는 것을 말해요. 사건, 사고, 통계 이야기가 나오는 뉴스에서 많이 써요. '다시 조사하다'라고 풀어서 말해도 돼요.

phrases.en: The police are re-investigating the case.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '재조사'를 동사로 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 재조사.

phrases.en: The results of the re-investigation come out next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다시 조사한 뒤의 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the outcome after investigating again.

phrases.en: The numbers were wrong, so we looked into it again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say it.

explain_en: It is used when the first investigation was lacking or its result is hard to trust, so it is done again. It is common in news about cases, accidents and statistics. You can also say it plainly as '다시 조사하다'.

en: to be uncovered; to be caught

examples.en: I was caught speeding.
A shop that sold fake goods was exposed.

examples.ko: 시험에서 부정행위를 하다 적발되면 점수를 잃어요.
examples.en: If you are caught cheating on an exam, you lose your score.

examples.ko: 세금을 속인 회사가 적발되었다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that a company that cheated on taxes had been caught.

examples.ko: 몰래 쓰레기를 버리다가 적발되지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to get caught dumping trash secretly.
If you break the rules, you can be caught.

explain: 숨기던 잘못이나 법·규정을 어긴 일이 조사나 단속으로 드러났을 때 써요. 단속, 검사, 점검과 자주 같이 나와요. 그냥 들키는 일은 '들키다'가 일상에서 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I was caught in a drunk driving crackdown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경찰이나 기관의 단속에서 잘못이 드러났을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for being caught in a check by police or authorities.

phrases.en: The company that was caught has to pay a fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못이 드러난 가게나 회사를 가리키는 꾸밈말 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for a shop or company whose wrongdoing was exposed.

phrases.en: Luckily, no one was caught.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못이 드러나지 않고 지나갔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the wrongdoing was not found out.

explain_en: Used when a hidden wrongdoing or a violation of laws or rules comes to light through inspection or enforcement. It often pairs with 단속, 검사, and 점검. For simply being found out in daily life, 들키다 sounds more natural.

en: to be totaled; to be aggregated

examples.en: The voting results were tallied at night.

examples.ko: 올해 방문객은 모두 십만 명으로 집계됐어요.
examples.en: This year's visitors were counted at 100,000 in total.
Scores are totaled automatically by computer.
Looking at the tallied figures, it's down from last year.
The survey responses haven't been tallied yet.

examples.ko: 이번 달 판매량이 집계되면 알려 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll let you know once this month's sales are totaled.

explain: 흩어진 숫자를 모아서 합친 결과가 나올 때 써요. 'N명으로 집계되다'처럼 뉴스에서 숫자와 같이 많이 나와요. 사람이 합치는 쪽에서는 '집계하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The participants were totaled at 500 people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 숫자 뒤에 '으로 집계되다'를 붙여 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the news, '으로 집계되다' follows a number to state the result.

phrases.en: A staff member tallies the vote results.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 숫자를 모아 합치는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person who adds up the numbers.

phrases.en: The vote count finished late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '집계'를 써서 합치는 일이 끝났다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '집계' to say the counting is finished.

explain_en: Use it when scattered numbers have been gathered and added up into a result. In the news it often comes with a number, as in 'N명으로 집계되다' (counted at N people). From the side of the person who adds them up, use '집계하다'.

en: prison break; jailbreak; escape from prison

examples.en: In the movie, the main character succeeds in breaking out of prison.
I like movies with prison break scenes.

examples.ko: 그 소설은 탈옥을 계획한 사람들의 이야기예요.
examples.en: That novel is a story about people who plan a prison escape.

examples.ko: 탈옥 후 며칠 만에 다시 붙잡혔대요.
examples.en: I heard he was caught again a few days after escaping.
Stories of escapes are passed down about old prisons.
Breaking out of prison is a serious crime in any country.

explain: '탈출'은 어디에서든 빠져나오는 일이고, '탈옥'은 감옥에서 도망치는 일에만 써요. 탈옥한 사람은 '탈옥수'라고 하고, 영화나 소설, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The prisoner escaped from prison at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '탈옥'에 '하다'를 붙여 실제로 도망친다고 말하는 동사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form with '하다' for actually escaping from prison.

phrases.en: The police caught the escaped prisoner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감옥에서 도망친 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who escaped from prison.

phrases.en: They failed to break out and were caught again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도망치지 못했다고 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for failing to get away.

explain_en: '탈출' is escaping from anywhere, while '탈옥' is only for escaping from prison. A person who escaped is called a '탈옥수', and the word often appears in films, novels and news.

en: to be made clear; to be proved

examples.ko: 검사 결과 소문은 사실이 아닌 것으로 판명됐어요.
examples.en: The test results proved the rumor was not true.

examples.ko: 새 제품이 기준을 통과하지 못하는 것으로 판명되어 출시를 미뤘어요.
examples.en: The new product turned out to fail the standard, so the launch was delayed.

examples.ko: 범인이 다른 사람으로 판명되면 어떻게 될까요?
examples.en: What happens if the culprit turns out to be someone else?

examples.ko: 나중에 그의 말이 모두 거짓으로 판명되었어요.
examples.en: Later, all his words turned out to be lies.
Don't use it until the cause is determined.
The cause of the accident hasn't been determined yet.

explain: 모르던 일이 조사나 검사 뒤에 분명하게 드러날 때 써요. '~으로 판명되다'의 형태로 자주 쓰고, 뉴스와 보고서에서 많이 나와요. 일상에서는 '밝혀지다'나 '알고 보니 ~이다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The rumor turned out to be true.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 뒤에 확실해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something becomes certain after investigation.

phrases.en: The cause of the accident was revealed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more natural word in daily speech.

phrases.en: I'll let you know after the result is confirmed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분명해진 다음의 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about what comes after things become clear.

explain_en: It is used when something unknown becomes clear after an investigation or test. It commonly takes the form '~으로 판명되다' and appears often in news and reports. In everyday talk, '밝혀지다' or '알고 보니 ~이다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The jury delivered a unanimous not-guilty verdict.

examples.ko: 평결이 나오기 전까지 모두 긴장하고 있었어요.
examples.en: Everyone was tense until the verdict came out.
When the verdict was announced, the courtroom went quiet.
It took the jurors three days to reach a verdict.

examples.ko: 이 사건의 평결은 다음 주에 나와요.
examples.en: The verdict in this case will come out next week.
I checked the content of the verdict in a news article.

explain: 배심원단이나 심사위원단이 모여서 내리는 판단을 말해요. 판사가 내리는 '판결'과 구별하고, '평결을 내리다/평결이 나오다'로 써요.

phrases.en: The jury delivered a not-guilty verdict for the defendant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재판 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말로, 무죄라는 판단을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in trial news, meaning a judgment of not guilty.

phrases.en: When the guilty verdict came out, the courtroom went quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무죄 평결'의 반대로, 죄가 있다는 판단이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 무죄 평결: a judgment that someone is guilty.

phrases.en: Everyone waited for the verdict, feeling nervous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과가 나오기 전의 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the situation before the result is announced.

explain_en: It refers to a judgment reached by a jury or panel together. Keep it distinct from '판결', which a judge delivers, and use it as '평결을 내리다/평결이 나오다'.

t90.ax: Everyone was tense until the verdict came out.

examples.en: Please write your current address accurately on the form.

examples.ko: 이 책은 한국 교육의 현주소를 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This book shows the current state of Korean education.
This is the current state of our society.

examples.ko: 현주소를 알아야 앞으로 계획을 세울 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to know where you stand now to make plans.
I checked where my skills stand now with a mock exam.

examples.ko: 이 기사는 청년 취업의 현주소를 다뤄요.
examples.en: This article covers the current situation of youth employment.

explain: 서류에서는 지금 살고 있는 주소를 뜻하고, 옛 주소나 본적과 구분할 때 써요. 일상에서는 오히려 '~의 현주소'처럼 지금의 상태나 수준을 말하는 비유로 더 많이 나와요. 말로 집 주소를 물을 때는 그냥 '주소'라고 해요.

phrases.en: This statistic is the current state of youth unemployment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일의 지금 모습이나 수준을 그대로 보여 줄 때 써요. 주로 뉴스나 글에서 나오고, 좋지 않은 현실을 말할 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to show the present state or level of something as it really is. It appears mostly in news and writing, often about an unfavorable reality.

explain_en: On forms it means the address where you live now, as distinct from an old address or registered domicile. In daily use it appears more often figuratively, as '~의 현주소', meaning the current state or level of something. When asking for a home address in speech, people just say '주소'.

examples.ko: 회사 돈을 횡령한 직원이 경찰에 잡혔어요.
examples.en: The employee who embezzled company money was caught by the police.

examples.ko: 횡령 사건 뉴스가 오늘 아침에 나왔어요.
examples.en: The news about the embezzlement case came out this morning.

examples.ko: 그는 횡령 혐의로 재판을 받고 있어요.
examples.en: He is on trial on charges of embezzlement.

examples.ko: 횡령 때문에 회사가 큰 손해를 입었어요.
examples.en: The company suffered a big loss because of the embezzlement.
Embezzlement was found at the bank and an investigation began.
They say the embezzled amount is as much as 500 million won.

explain: '절도'는 남의 것을 몰래 가져가는 것이고, '횡령'은 맡아서 관리하던 돈이나 물건을 내 것처럼 쓰는 거예요. 회사 돈, 단체 돈과 함께 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그는 횡령 혐의로 조사를 받고 있어요.
phrases.en: He is being investigated on suspicion of embezzlement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase in the news.

phrases.example: 회삿돈을 마음대로 쓰면 횡령죄가 될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Using company money freely can be the crime of embezzlement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 횡령이 법에서 죄가 될 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when embezzlement counts as a crime under the law.

phrases.en: The public funds embezzlement case became widely known.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단체나 나라의 돈을 몰래 쓴 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to secretly using money that belongs to an organization or the state.

explain_en: '절도' is secretly taking someone else's property, while '횡령' is using money or goods you were entrusted to manage as if they were your own. It often appears in the news with company or organization funds.

examples.en: The Far East region is very cold in winter.

examples.ko: 러시아 극동에는 큰 항구 도시가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a large port city in the Russian Far East.

examples.ko: 유럽 사람들은 옛날에 한국과 일본을 극동이라고 불렀어요.
examples.en: In the past, Europeans called Korea and Japan the Far East.
The situation in the Far East often appears in the news.

examples.ko: 극동 쪽으로 가는 비행기는 자리가 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Flights heading to the Far East don't have many seats.
Merchants from the Far East gathered at the market.

explain: 유럽에서 본 동쪽 끝이라는 관점에서 나온 말이라, 요즘은 '동아시아'를 더 많이 써요. 러시아 '극동 지역'처럼 뉴스나 역사 이야기에서 주로 만나요.

phrases.en: In the Far East region, winter is very long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말로, 특히 러시아 동쪽 끝 지역을 가리킬 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common pairing and is often used for the far eastern region of Russia.

phrases.en: In the past, there were many merchants who came from the Far East.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에서'를 붙여 어디에서 왔는지, 어디에서 일어났는지 말할 때 써요. 역사 이야기에 잘 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 에서, it says where someone came from or where something happened, and it appears often in history talk.
phrases.en_equiv: in or from the Far East

phrases.en: Korea and Japan are in East Asia.
phrases.nuance_ko: '극동'과 비슷한 지역을 가리키지만, 요즘은 이쪽을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It points to a similar area as 극동, but it is the more common word today.

explain_en: This word comes from a European viewpoint of the eastern edge, so '동아시아' is used more often today. You mostly meet it in news and history, as in Russia's '극동 지역'.
